Let
\[
B((u,v),(u',v'))=u\cdot v'+u'\cdot v\in\mathbb F_2 .
\]
For a compatible twist write \(\theta_x=(-1)^{q(x)}\). The twist condition is exactly
\[
q(x+y)=q(x)+q(y)+B(x,y),
\]
so compatible twists are quadratic refinements of \(B\). Since
\[
q_0(u,v)=u\cdot v
\]
is one such refinement and \(B\) is nondegenerate, every twist is uniquely
\[
q_z(x)=q_0(x)+B(z,x),\qquad z\in V.
\]

An \(m\)-dimensional subspace \(L\) is Lagrangian for \(q\) iff \(q|_L=0\). Then automatically \(B|_L=0\), so \(L=L^\perp\).

Now fix an ordered triple \((q,q_1,q_2)\), and write
\[
q_1=q+B(d_1,-),\qquad q_2=q+B(d_2,-).
\]
The twists are pairwise distinct iff \(d_1,d_2\) are nonzero and distinct, hence linearly independent over \(\mathbb F_2\). If \(L\) is common Lagrangian, then for every \(x\in L\),
\[
B(d_i,x)=q_i(x)+q(x)=0,
\]
so \(d_i\in L^\perp=L\). Thus \(L\) must contain
\[
W=\langle d_1,d_2\rangle.
\]
Conversely, if \(L\) is \(q\)-Lagrangian and contains \(W\), then \(q_1,q_2\) also vanish on \(L\). Hence the count is the number of \(q\)-Lagrangians containing \(W\).

This is possible exactly when \(W\) is totally \(q\)-singular:
\[
q(d_1)=q(d_2)=q(d_1+d_2)=0,
\]
equivalently \(q(d_1)=q(d_2)=0\) and \(B(d_1,d_2)=0\). Also \(q\) must be of plus type, i.e. must admit an \(m\)-dimensional totally singular subspace.

For plus type in dimension \(2n\), the number \(A_n\) of maximal totally singular \(n\)-subspaces is
\[
A_n=2\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}(2^i+1).
\]
Indeed \(A_1=2\), and double-counting pairs \((L,a)\) with \(0\ne a\in L\) gives
\[
A_n(2^n-1)
=(2^{2n-1}+2^{n-1}-1)A_{n-1}
=(2^n-1)(2^{n-1}+1)A_{n-1}.
\]
Thus \(A_n=(2^{n-1}+1)A_{n-1}\).

Here \(W\) has dimension \(2\), so the quotient \(W^\perp/W\) has plus type and dimension \(2(m-2)\). Therefore the maximum common count is
\[
M_m=A_{m-2}=2\prod_{i=1}^{m-3}(2^i+1).
\]

It remains to count ordered triples attaining this maximum.

The plus twists are exactly those \(q_z\) with \(q_0(z)=0\), so their number is
\[
2^{2m-1}+2^{m-1}.
\]
For a fixed plus twist \(q\), the number of ordered pairs \((d_1,d_2)\) giving a totally singular \(2\)-plane is:
\[
(2^{2m-1}+2^{m-1}-1)(2^{2m-2}+2^{m-1}-2).
\]
The first factor chooses a nonzero singular \(d_1\). For fixed \(d_1\), the quotient \(d_1^\perp/\langle d_1\rangle\) is plus type of dimension \(2m-2\), so the number of singular \(d_2\in d_1^\perp\), excluding \(0,d_1\), is
\[
2(2^{2m-3}+2^{m-2})-2
=
2^{2m-2}+2^{m-1}-2.
\]

Hence
\[
N_m=
(2^{2m-1}+2^{m-1})
(2^{2m-1}+2^{m-1}-1)
(2^{2m-2}+2^{m-1}-2).
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
(M_m,N_m)=
\left(
2\prod_{i=1}^{m-3}(2^i+1),
\ (2^{2m-1}+2^{m-1})(2^{2m-1}+2^{m-1}-1)(2^{2m-2}+2^{m-1}-2)
\right)
}
\]
for every \(m\ge 3\).
